saw.short: John Lewis's ad is still the week's big talking point
saw.headline: The John Lewis ad is *still the week’s big debate*
saw.what: System1 says the ad scores 5.6 stars, its best John Lewis result since 2019, with 69% reacting positively and 6% showing contempt. That is System1’s own research, shared by its Chief Growth Officer in The Drum. Metro’s columnist says the culture-war backlash is louder than the numbers.
saw.why: It started the week as a pile-on. The testing says most viewers liked it.

saw.short: KFC's Doom menu and the Hunger Games stunt: two film tie-ins
saw.headline: Two film tie-ins: *KFC’s Doom menu* and a *Hunger Games* TV stunt
saw.what: KFC’s Doctor Doom menu, with a black sesame bun burger, reaches UK and Ireland restaurants on 9 Nov, ahead of Avengers: Doomsday. Eastern Eye gives the film’s UK date as 16 Dec. Earlier this week viewers also saw an in-universe Hunger Games clip in US election coverage, per indy100. Sunrise on the Reaping opens on 20 Nov, per listings.
saw.why: Two ways to sell a film: a menu and a stunt in a moment everyone watches.
saw.source: Eastern Eye, 5 Nov; Decision Marketing, 4 Nov; indy100, 4 Nov

saw.short: Arsenal's Christmas film stars Colin Firth
saw.headline: *Colin Firth* stars in Arsenal’s Christmas film
saw.what: Arsenal’s Christmas film, “’Twas the Season”, has Colin Firth as a fan walking through Islington crowds, with Alessia Russo, Riccardo Calafiori and Gabriel Magalhães. Metro says Firth’s Portuguese exchange with the players nods to Love Actually. The tagline is “Gifts worth waiting all season for”.
saw.why: A football club making a proper Christmas ad. The cast does the work.

saw.short: Barbour's Christmas short brings back Wallace and Gromit
saw.headline: *Wallace and Gromit* star in Barbour’s Christmas short
saw.what: Barbour’s new 90-second Christmas short with Wallace and Gromit, made with Aardman, has Gromit rescuing Wallace’s Walk-o-Matic test. A mischievous sheep also appears. A Metro writer calls it his favourite ad so far, though a colleague prefers another.
saw.why: Familiar characters, a clear story and a very British feel. Opinion is split on the best ad.

saw.short: Boots' Christmas ad goes to TV
saw.headline: *Boots* takes its Christmas campaign to TV
saw.what: Boots’ campaign, “For Gifts They’ll Really Love”, went online on 4 Nov and goes to TV on 6 Nov, under its new “Give it Some Boots” platform. It is a 60-second film, with the brand’s first 20-second edits. Retail Gazette says the TV roadblock aims to reach six million people over launch weekend.
saw.why: A big TV launch weekend. The first 20-second edits are the detail to note.

saw.short: GTA 6 has an estimated 7.71 million pre-orders
saw.headline: *GTA 6* has an estimated *7.71 million* pre-orders
saw.what: Sensor Tower estimates 7.71 million pre-orders for GTA 6, worth about $751 million, ahead of its 19 Nov launch. GamesIndustry.biz and Metro both report the figure. It is Sensor Tower’s estimate of digital pre-orders, not a Take-Two number.
saw.why: Two weeks out, a game is already a cultural event. Expect it to fill feeds from 19 Nov.

platform.headline: Instagram’s *Edits* video editor comes to Mac
platform.what: Edits now has a Mac app, launched on 5 Nov. Social Media Today and TechCrunch say it has a multi-track timeline, 4K watermark-free export and syncs with the mobile app. UK availability isn’t stated.
platform.why: Easier editing on a laptop for anyone making Reels.
platform.source: Social Media Today, 5 Nov; TechCrunch, 5 Nov

platform.short: Meta's Muse AI can now talk, US first
platform.headline: Meta’s *Muse AI* can now talk, US first
platform.what: Meta says its Muse AI assistant now has voice and expressive avatars, with hundreds of voices to choose from. It is rolling out in the US first, so it isn’t in the UK yet. Meta says voice is coming soon to its AI glasses.
platform.why: A signal of where Meta’s AI is going. Nothing to use in the UK yet.
platform.source: Meta, 5 Nov; Social Media Today, 5 Nov
